final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence; the response reframed the same record more narrowly and, in material respects, conceded the original concerns. That narrower framing is analytically better than an uncaveated certification claim, but it is still not enough for compliant_with_caveats on this record because the caveat is itself an unresolved compliance predicate. The governing policy and policy text require that, when the named use case remains exposed, the material limitation must either be disclosed before launch or be covered by reviewed/approved risk acceptance. Admissible evidence shows operational readiness at an aggregate level, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and staged rollout with rollback. Admissible evidence also shows the aviation maintenance triage segment is below target, remains in the initial cohort, and lacks approved risk acceptance. What is still missing is proof that the required disclosure package actually exists in final pre-launch form and governs launch. Because the Actor's revised position depends on a condition not shown in evidence, the support gap remains unresolved. This is therefore still suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats: a caveated path may be possible, but present compliance has not been evidenced.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows a final pre-launch model-card or equivalent disclosure artifact that explicitly names the aviation maintenance triage use case and its deferred-defect routing limitation.
No admissible evidence shows that any such disclosure artifact was reviewed, approved, or attached to the launch decision.
The affected aviation maintenance triage segment remains exposed in the initial random rollout cohort.
The only risk-acceptance artifact in evidence is incomplete: the approver line is blank and it does not address the exposed aviation maintenance triage segment.
Rollout controls, 6% initial exposure, monitoring, and rollback are operational mitigations, not substitutes for the disclosure-or-approved-risk-acceptance predicate in policy.
